title: Rails Routing
intro: Rails routing is the map between URLs and controller actions, and understanding it deeply is the difference between a developer who scaffolds routes and one who designs them. This page covers the seven RESTful routes that resources generates, nested routes and the two-level depth rule, member vs collection routes, namespace vs scope vs module, route constraints with regex and custom constraint objects, named routes and path/url helpers, and mounting Rack apps and engines. The routing interview question often comes in scenario form: 'your URL is 404 even though the route is in routes.rb — what do you check?' — and the answer requires understanding how Rails routes are matched top-to-bottom.
